chunks: Have trust in the Living One who will never die, and sing His hallelujas; for He is well aware of the sins of His creatures.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to trust in the Ever-Living God according to Surah Al-Furqan?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to emphasize the attribute of 'Al-Hayy' (The Ever-Living) as the ultimate source of stability, contrasting with the transient nature of worldly powers. The phrase 'wa kafa bihi' (and He is sufficient) is interpreted by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai as indicating that Allah’s comprehensive knowledge of human faults is not merely observational but sufficient to guide, forgive, and manage their affairs without need for external assistance. This reinforces the concept of divine sufficiency (kifayah) in times of spiritual or worldly uncertainty.
